FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
Suspension takes the license away for a time before return, possibly with a termination fee, while revocation cancels it outright so reapplication, possibly denied, starts over after the revocation term; the same fates apply to out-of-state driving privileges and to unlicensed permission. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=19]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
Junior permits and licenses draw a sixty-day suspension for a serious three-point-plus violation or two lesser ones, a sixty-day revocation for the same pattern within six months of restoration, one hundred twenty days for texting or cell-phone use, and the permit must be held six months before any road test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=19]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
Licensed adults eighteen or older serve six months of probation, where DWAI, speeding, reckless driving, tailgating, speed contests or any two violations trigger sixty days off plus a fresh six-month probation, a repeat round revokes at least six months with probation after restoration, and texting or cell-phone use costs one hundred twenty days. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=19]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
Ticketed drivers must answer promptly or face indefinite suspension and possible default conviction, and city tickets for non-criminal moving violations go through the Traffic Violations Bureau while criminal driving charges stay in the regular courts. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=19]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A02
Outside the city, traffic cases land in the city, county, town or village criminal and traffic court where the offense happened, and every ticketed motorist may mount a defense with a lawyer. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=20]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A02
Out-of-state moving convictions of non-commercial licensees go unrecorded except offenses in Ontario and Quebec, and only those two provinces feed the violation-point record. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=20]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A02
Ignoring an out-of-state moving ticket suspends the New York license until answered and proven satisfied, except tickets from Alaska, California, Michigan, Montana, Oregon, Virginia and Wisconsin, a list the text calls six states, with mirror suspension at home for other states drivers who snub a New York summons. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=20]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A02
Out-of-state or Canadian alcohol or drug driving convictions revoke New York licenses at least ninety days from age twenty-one up, at least one year or until twenty-one whichever runs longer below that age, and any-state criminal negligence, homicide or assault convictions from fatal driving revoke the license and possibly registrations too. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=20]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A02
Suspension and revocation have many mandatory triggers, and motorboat and snowmobile operators under twenty-one who drink face matching sanctions on those privileges. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=20]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A02
Aggravated DWI at point-one-eight blood alcohol revokes at least one year, plain DWI at point-zero-eight revokes at least six months, alcohol-impaired driving suspends ninety days, drug-impaired driving revokes at least six months, and out-of-state DUI revokes ninety days to six months by conviction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=20]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A03
Refusing a chemical test revokes at least one year past twenty-one, eighteen months with a refusal or alcohol or drug violation inside five years, at least one year for a first under-twenty-one refusal, until twenty-one or one year whichever is longer for a second, and at least one year for Zero Tolerance refusals. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=21]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A03
Under-twenty-one arrests ending in any listed alcohol or drug conviction revoke at least one year, a second while still under twenty-one runs one year or until twenty-one whichever is longer, and youthful-offender and out-of-state cases count the same. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=21]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A03
Zero Tolerance suspends under-twenty-one licenses six months for blood alcohol from point-zero-two to point-zero-seven, a level one drink can reach, and a second offense revokes one year or until twenty-one whichever is longer. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=21]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A03
Revocation of at least six months follows three speeding or misdemeanor traffic violations within eighteen months dated by offense, three stopped-school-bus passings within three years, one injury or fatal scene-leaving, or one speed contest, with a second contest inside twelve months stretching to at least one year. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=21]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A03
Driving or lending an uninsured vehicle, or crashing uninsured, revokes at least one year, lapsed coverage means surrendering plates and registration, and parked off-road vehicles still need their plates returned or civil and suspension penalties follow. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=21]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A03
Skipping a crash report, child support, taxes or a crash court judgment suspends indefinitely until the underlying condition is fixed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=21]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A03
The point system hunts persistent violators through a violation table that also governs public parking lots, single violations alone rarely force action except alcohol, drug or aggravated unlicensed cases, and every vehicle and traffic violation adds fines on top of license sanctions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=21]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A04
The table plainly pairs texting while driving, facilitating aggravated unlicensed operation, and leaving an injury scene at five points each, construction-zone speeding at eight, aggravated unlicensed operation and chemical-test refusals at eleven, child-restraint violations at three, and inadequate brakes on an employer vehicle at four. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=22]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A04
The same table also rates reckless driving, school-bus passing, railroad crossings, signal and sign disobedience, passing and lane faults, property-damage leaving, and most other moving violations, with speeding split into bands from one-to-ten through over forty miles over the limit. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=22]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A04
Points count from the offense date, eleven or more within twenty-four months brings a mailed suspension notice, and the only hearing argument is mistaken identity, never re-arguing guilt or pleading hardship. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=22]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A04
An approved crash-prevention course cuts up to four points and ten percent of liability and collision premiums, yet never stops a mandatory sanction, banks no future credit, and trims no responsibility assessment. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=22]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A04
Preventable crashes replaced accidents in the vocabulary, and a fatal crash can suspend or revoke after a hearing even with no violation charged at the scene. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=22]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A04
Fixed-term suspensions end only after a fifty-dollar termination fee, while Zero Tolerance suspensions demand a one-hundred-twenty-five-dollar civil penalty plus a one-hundred-dollar termination fee. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=22]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A05
Revocation usually requires a one-hundred-dollar reapplication fee, waived for no-insurance revocations and for conditional or restricted-use licenses. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=23]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A05
A twenty-nineteen law lets school districts and towns use bus stop-arm cameras against owners who pass a stopped loading bus with reds flashing, fining two hundred fifty dollars first, twenty-seven second within eighteen months, and three hundred third and beyond within eighteen months, as extracted. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=23]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A05
Before relicensing after revocation, uninsured operation or crashes cost a seven-hundred-fifty-dollar civil penalty, refusals five hundred or five hundred fifty in a commercial vehicle, and repeat-alcohol refusals within five years seven hundred fifty. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=23]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A05
Aggravated DWI, DWI, any DWAI variant, or a chemical refusal each trigger a yearly two-hundred-fifty-dollar responsibility assessment for three years, on top of all other fines, with non-payment suspending every credential. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=23]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A05
Six points inside eighteen months trigger one hundred dollars yearly for three years plus twenty-five per extra point per year, the assessment reaches motorboat and snowmobile cases at times, and no crash-prevention course shrinks it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=23]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A05
Suspended or revoked driving is criminal with two-hundred-to-five-thousand-dollar fines plus possible jail or probation and vehicle seizure, worse when intoxicated on an alcohol suspension, severe past ten ticket-ignoring suspensions, and criminal past twenty even without driving at arrest. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=23]
